paper_id: Greenplum_ A Hybrid Database for Transactional and Analytical Workloads
title: Greenplum: A Hybrid Database for Transactional and Analytical Workloads
motivation: Enterprise users want a single system for both OLTP and OLAP workloads, reducing complexity of maintaining separate systems
problem_framing: Adding OLTP capability to an OLAP data warehouse while maintaining ACID properties with minimal performance overhead
key_insight: Design decisions favoring OLAP workloads (two-phase commit, restrictive locking) become prohibitively expensive for OLTP — small overhead accumulates significantly for short queries
method_signature: Global Deadlock Detector + One-Phase Commit + Resource Groups for OLTP/OLAP isolation
evaluation_criteria: TPC-B TPS, CH-benCHmark mixed workload throughput (QPH/QPM), scalability with client connections
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: OLAP performance slows 2x in GPDB 6 due to OLTP resource preemption; throughput declines beyond 600 clients due to LWLock bottleneck
evidence_for_taste: seemingly insignificant overhead becomes quite significant
first step and more work is needed
thinking_moves: 从性能瓶颈反推底层设计问题: two-phase commit和restrictive locking对短查询影响大
识别看似微小的开销在短事务场景下的累积效应
通过benchmark数据量变化揭示PostgreSQL vs Greenplum的本质差异
承认当前优化只是第一步，性能仍无法比肩专用OLTP数据库
